H5800.d: to loosen, i.e. relinquish, permit, etc.

H5869.d: an eye (literally or figuratively); by analogy, a fountain (as the eye of the landscape)

H5892.d: a city (a place guarded by waking or a watch) in the widest sense (even of a mere encampment or post)

fb: Man living at the time before the Flood
Cain's grandson through Enoch and Mehujael's father. His line runs on to Lamech and the culture-founders Jabal, Jubal and Tubal-cain.
Gaza, under a more literal spelling. The southernmost of the five chief Philistine cities, it sat on the coastal road between Egypt and Canaan.

H5867.d: Elam, a son of Shem and his descendants, with their country; also of six Israelites
fb: A kingdom east of Babylon. In the prophets it is one of the nations among which God scattered Israel. Its people turn up again at Pentecost.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
The head of a family that came back from Babylon, counted in Ezra 2 and Nehemiah 7. Some of his descendants were in the foreign-marriage list of Ezra 10.
Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
One of 7 men called Elam. This one is a man from the patriarchs, named twice in Genesis and 1 Chronicles.
Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A levite from the divided-kingdom years. 1 Chronicles names him once.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 1 Chronicles is the only book that names him.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Nehemiah names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
One of 7 men called Elam. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Nehemiah.

H5857.d: Ai, Aja or Ajath, a place in Palestine
fb: A fortified Canaanite city near Bethel. Israel's first attack was thrown back because of Achan's hidden sin, and once that was dealt with Joshua took the city by ambush. The site is usually identified with et-Tell, though digging there has turned up little from the right period.
Named once, in Jeremiah, and nowhere else.
Spring of judgment, the old name for Kadesh in the wilderness south of Canaan. Chedorlaomer's kings hit it on the campaign that ended with Abram chasing them to get Lot back.

H5861.d: a hawk or other bird of prey

H5891.d: Ephah, the name of a son of Midian, and of the region settled by him; also of an Israelite and of an Israelitess
fb: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
Midian's son and Abraham's grandson through Keturah. His people settled in northern Arabia, and Isaiah pictures the land of Ephah bringing gold and incense to Zion.
Named once, in Isaiah, and nowhere else.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 4 men called Ephah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1 Chronicles names her once, and she is a woman from the divided-kingdom years.

H5848.d: to shroud, i.e. clothe (whether transitive or reflex.); hence (from the idea of darkness) to languish

H5895.d: properly, a young ass (as just broken to a load); hence an ass-colt

fb: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs

The mountain of the curses, opposite Mount Gerizim near Shechem. Moses ordered six tribes onto Ebal to speak the covenant's curses while six on Gerizim spoke its blessings, and Joshua built an altar there and wrote the law on stones. A Horite chief descended from Seir carried the name too.

H5879.d: Enajim or Enam, a place in Palestine
fb: Tamar sat veiled at Enaim and waited for Judah, who had not given her his youngest son. The name means two springs, or two eyes, and the spot is usually placed between Adullam and Timnah.

H5826.d: to surround, i.e. protect or aid

H5816.d: Uzziel, the name of six Israelites
fb: Aaron's uncle living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Kohath's son, and Aaron's uncle. His descendants had their own duties at the tabernacle.
Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A levite from the divided-kingdom years, and 1 Chronicles is the only book that names him.
Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A levite from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Nehemiah names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
Warrior living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
One of 6 men called Uzziel. This one is a warrior from the wilderness years, named once in 1 Chronicles.

H5844.d: to wrap, i.e. cover, veil, clothe, or roll

fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Father of Naphtali's tribal leader in the wilderness census, and nothing else is recorded.

H5817.d: an Uzzielite (collectively) or descendants of Uzziel
fb: Aaron's uncle living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
The Levitical clan from Uzziel, one of the four Kohathite families. Under David some of them kept the temple treasuries.
They camped here on the border of Moab late in the journey from Egypt. The name means "ruins of Abarim", after the range east of the Jordan, and the camp itself has not been found.

H5852.d: Ataroth, the name (thus simply) of two places in Palestine
fb: Named twice, in Joshua, and nowhere else.
Reuben and Gad asked for Ataroth because the pasture was good for their livestock. Several towns east of the Jordan shared the name.
Short for Atroth-shophan, a town in Gilead that Gad rebuilt and fortified. Its site is unknown.

H5864.d: Ijim, a place in the Desert.
fb: The name means ruins, and two places carry it. One is a town in the far south of Judah near Edom; the other is a late stop in the wilderness, just before Israel reached Moab's border.

H5871.d: Ajin, the name (thus simply) of two places in Palestine
fb: Given to Simeon inside Judah's territory, and later made one of the cities handed to the Levites.
Named once, in Numbers, and nowhere else.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Paltiel's father, named only so we know whose son the Issachar leader was when the land of Canaan was divided.

A fortified town in Judah's Shephelah. Joshua routed five Amorite kings near it in a hailstorm. A Lachish ostracon written during Nebuchadnezzar's last campaign says the writer is watching for Lachish's signal fires but cannot see Azekah, which some read as Azekah already fallen and others as a line of sight he never had.

H5841.d: an Azzathite or inhabitant of Azzah
fb: A man of Gaza. Judges uses it for the men who waited at the gate to kill Samson, and he carried the gate off.
A spring on the road down toward Jericho, not far from Bethany, marking the line between Judah and Benjamin. The name means fountain of the sun, and a spring still flows on that route.

A spring just south of Jerusalem where the Kidron and Hinnom valleys meet. Jonathan and Ahimaaz waited there to carry news to David in Absalom's revolt, and Adonijah held his feast there to make himself king. Many put it at Bir Ayyub, Job's Well.
Fountain of gardens. This one sat on Issachar's border and went to the Gershonite Levites, and it is generally identified with Jenin, which still has the name and its springs.
Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

An oasis on the western shore of the Dead Sea, fed by a spring that drops some 600 feet down the cliffs. David hid in its caves from Saul and spared Saul's life there. A Chalcolithic temple on the site is far older than Israel in Canaan.
A town on the line between Ephraim and Benjamin, in Joshua's boundary lists twice, and no confident modern identification has been made.
The spring by Tappuah that marked the line between Ephraim and Manasseh. The town went to Ephraim though it stood on Manasseh's land.
Home of the medium Saul went to in disguise the night before his last battle. It lay in Issachar's land, near where Deborah and Barak beat Sisera. Endur, southeast of Mount Tabor, keeps the name.
A town on Issachar's border, next to Engannim in the list, with no site found.
A fortified town of Naphtali, not the big city of Hazor, named once with its site lost.
Named twice, in 1 Chronicles, and nowhere else.
The rock of Etam, where Samson went down into a cleft and stayed after he had cut down the Philistines.
2 Chronicles names him once, and nothing else is recorded.
Spring of the one who called, the water God opened at Lehi for Samson after the jawbone fight.

H5860.d: to swoop down upon (literally or figuratively)

H5849.d: to encircle (for attack or protection); especially to crown (literally or figuratively)

H5896.d: Ira, the name of three Israelites
fb: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
One of David's elite warriors, who in Chronicles also commands one of the monthly army divisions. Ira was the name of more than one of David's men.
Man living at the time of United Monarchy
2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the united kingdom.
Man living at the time of United Monarchy
One of 3 men called Ira. This one is a man from the united kingdom, named once in 2 Samuel.

H5820.d: Azmaveth, the name of three Israelites and of a place in Palestine
fb: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
He fought for David and made the list of David's thirty. The same name belonged to a town near Jerusalem and to several other men. His own record is a line in each of the two lists of the thirty.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1 Chronicles names him twice, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 4 men called Azmaveth. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 1 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

H5838.d: Azarjah, the name of nineteen Israelites
fb: Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
This is King Uzziah of Judah under his other name.
Daniel's compatriot living at the time of Exile and Return
Abednego's birth name. He was one of Daniel's three friends thrown into the fiery furnace in Babylon for refusing to worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden image.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
An Azariah in Nehemiah's lists, at 7:7, 10:2 and 12:33. The name was common and nothing more is known of him.
Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A priest in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles 6, named again at Ezra 7:3, and neither the king nor Daniel's friend.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1 Chronicles names him twice, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him. The verses are 2 Chronicles 31:10 and 2 Chronicles 31:13.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A man from the exile and the return. Nehemiah names him twice.
Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 17 men called Azariah. This one is a priest from the divided-kingdom years, named twice in 2 Chronicles.
Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
A priest from the united kingdom. 1 Kings and 1 Chronicles name him twice.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 17 men called Azariah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A man from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 17 men called Azariah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him. The verse is 2 Chronicles 29:12.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A man from the exile and the return. Nehemiah names him once.
Man living at the time of United Monarchy
1 Kings names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.
Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A prophet from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

In Naphtali, in Israel's far north. Ben-hadad took it at Asa's request, and later Tiglath-pileser III took it in Pekah's reign, a conquest his own inscriptions also list. It is usually identified with Tell Dibbin.

H5806.d: Azubah, the name of two Israelitesses
fb: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1 Chronicles names her twice, and she is a woman from the divided-kingdom years.
Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
Jehoshaphat's mother. Kings and Chronicles both name her in the notice of his reign and give her nothing more.

H5818.d: Uzzijah, the name of five Israelites
fb: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

King of Judah at sixteen, he reigned fifty-two years and rebuilt the army and the economy. Then he went into the temple to burn incense himself, which no king was allowed to do. The priests confronted him and leprosy broke out on his forehead while he stood there.
Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a Levite from the divided-kingdom years.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 5 men called Uzziah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A man from the exile and the return, and Ezra is the only book that names him.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A man from the exile and the return. Nehemiah names him once.
Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
Jerahmeel's second wife and mother of Onam.

One of the place-clans listed under Salma in Judah's genealogy, beside Bethlehem and the Netophathites. The awkward wording is probably a compound name, Atroth-beth-Joab, to tell this Ataroth from the others. Nobody has found it.

H5840.d: Azrikam, the name of four Israelites
fb: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
He was a palace official, killed alongside King Ahaz's son when the invasion came.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of several men with this name, this one listed twice in the same family line, at 1 Chronicles 8:38 and again at 9:44.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 4 men called Azrikam. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

H5829.d: Ezer, the name of four Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 5 men called Ezer. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Named once, in the genealogies of 1 Chronicles 4. The Seirite chief and the Ephraimite with the same name are other men.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the wilderness years.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A man from the exile and the return. Nehemiah names him once.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A Levite who repaired a stretch of Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
Father of Jether, Mered, Epher and Jalon, in a Judah genealogy that also names Mered's wives and some descendants tied to Egypt, and nothing more is recorded of Ezrah himself.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A Reubenite east of the Jordan, Bela's father. Nothing further is recorded of him.

H5837.d: Azriel, the name of three Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A tribal leader of Manasseh, named once in Chronicles.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A tribal leader of Manasseh carries the name, and so does the father of an official Jehoiakim sent to arrest Jeremiah.

H5813.d: Uzzi, the name of six Israelites
fb: Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
There are several. This one sits in the high priestly line in 1 Chronicles 6, and Ezra 7:4 traces Ezra back through him.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1 Chronicles names him twice, and he is a man from the wilderness years.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A man from the exile and the return, and 1 Chronicles is the only book that names him.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A man from the exile and the return. Nehemiah names him once.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Nehemiah names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
One of 7 men called Uzzi. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Nehemiah.
Warrior living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
One of 7 men called Uzzi. This one is a warrior from the wilderness years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
A hard verse in Benjamin's genealogy, and many read this name as a variant of Iri, Bela's son a few verses earlier. Nothing else is known.
Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
An Ahohite among David's chief warriors. Samuel's list has Zalmon in his place.
Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of David's mighty men, from Ashtaroth in Bashan, east of the Jordan.

H5832.d: Azarel, the name of five Israelites
fb: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
Chronicles names him once, among David's musicians and officers.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of several men called Azarel in Chronicles, this one in the list at 1 Chronicles 12:6.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 6 men called Azarael. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A man from the exile and the return, and Ezra is the only book that names him.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Nehemiah names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
Priest living at the time of Exile and Return
A priest from the exile and the return. Nehemiah names him once.
Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy
He played the psaltery when the ark was brought up to Jerusalem. The name seems to be short for Jaaziel, two verses earlier in the same list.

H5812.d: Azazjah, the name of three Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of the musicians appointed under David, at 1 Chronicles 15:21.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A Levitical name. One Azaziah was a musician under David; this one is an overseer in the temple stores.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
He was Chelub's son, and David put him over the workers who farmed the royal land; that one line in Chronicles is the whole of him.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A large family among the returning exiles carried his name, listed by household in Ezra and Nehemiah both.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Nehemiah names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
Priest living at the time of Exile and Return
The priest and scribe who led a second return from exile, from Babylon to Jerusalem. In Nehemiah 8 he reads the law aloud to the whole assembled people, and they weep.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
He is not the famous scribe but a priest in Nehemiah's list of those who came back earlier under Zerubbabel, and he is named only there.
Priest living at the time of Exile and Return
The priest and scribe who led a second return from exile, from Babylon to Jerusalem. In Nehemiah 8 he reads the law aloud to the whole assembled people, and they weep.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
He is not the famous scribe but a priest in Nehemiah's list of those who came back earlier under Zerubbabel, and he is named only there.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Ezra 10:27 names him in Zattu's family, one of the men who had married a foreign wife after the return and had to send her away under Ezra's reforms.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
There are two Nehemiahs, and Azbuk fathered the other one, who ruled half the district of Beth-zur and repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall. He is there only to name his son.

H5809.d: Azzur, the name of three Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
Jeremiah names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
One of 3 men called Azur. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Ezekiel.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
He signed the covenant under Nehemiah, and that is all the record holds of him. The name, properly Azzur, means he that assists.
Spring of the pomegranate, a Negev town resettled after the exile. It likely joins Ain and Rimmon, which the older tribal lists name separately.

H5845.d: a receptacle (for milk, i.e. pail; figuratively, breast)

H5808.d: forcible; collectively and concretely, an army

H5801.d: trade, i.e. the place (mart) or the payment (revenue)

fb: In Ezekiel's vision the healed Dead Sea will have fishermen spreading nets from En-gedi to En-eglaim. The name means spring of the two calves, and it has never been firmly located.
Daniel's compatriot living at the time of Exile and Return
Abednego's birth name. He was one of Daniel's three friends thrown into the fiery furnace in Babylon for refusing to worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden image.

H5894.d: a watcher, i.e. an angel (as guardian)
